reviewComments.body: For fork pull requests under GitHub's default token restrictions, `pull_request` workflows receive a read-only token despite `pull-requests: write`. Decorating a bare title therefore fails at `gh pr edit`. Use `pull_request_target` for this metadata-only workflow, retaining checkout's trusted base revision; never check out or execute PR-head code with the write token.

Changing an already decorated title from `feat` to `fix` while retaining `:sparkles:` leaves the wrong gitmoji: any recognized prefix is accepted, so `updateTitle` skips the edit. Replace prefixes that do not match the parsed type, while preserving matching shortcode or Unicode prefixes. Add a regression test for changing types.

operatorItems: none: the pull request carries no operator comment or review; the only review is the automated one above

routing.subject: fork pull requests receive a read-only token, so gh pr edit cannot decorate their titles
routing.reason: Already boarded by VER-001 with the same cause. The suggested pull_request_target trigger cannot serve this order: that event runs the workflow file from the base branch, and main holds no workflow until this change merges, so the published pull request would get no title run at all. D010 names the two routes; choosing one is the next repair, after the merge.

routing.subject: a decorated title whose type changes keeps the old gitmoji because any recognized prefix is accepted
routing.target: FINAL-001 F1, repaired in this review (WO-004-D015)
routing.reason: Reproduced: decorateTitle(":sparkles: fix: x") returned the title unchanged. decorateTitle now keeps a prefix only when it is the shortcode or emoji of the title's own type and otherwise replaces it; two regression tests cover the change of type through decorateTitle and through updateTitle.
